doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: De De's first brass band with Gunye
summary: De De recalls his cousin Dejean's brass band, its members, music and marching tempos.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Oh, did he? I forgot to ask you something. What was the first brass band you played with? I don't know. I know it was. I sure remember.

I don't want to start playing with the boys. Let me see where the... In the Jefferson Boys? Yeah Jefferson City Boys, I mean the bass band. Yeah, he's playing for the... I can't follow that man's name. Rene, how much? Wait a minute, I called his name this morning. Corpintuck. Wait a minute. He did, uh... Dejama Gunye. Yeah, Dejama Gunye. He had, uh... That was my cousin. Yeah, your cousin. Yeah. He was the first man over here. We had, uh... He was called the Gunye's band, or I could remember the brass band at that time. Called the what? Gunye. Gunye. Gunye. He was the trumpet man. He's the one who had the band in charge for his brass band I had. I mean, I worked with... I worked with him for years.
And who was in that band?

Who? Shoo. How many of them? Eleven men at that time. They touched that time. Book, cool, old, ripped. Buck, what all they did. Bucku? I had a gun. I had a gun. Henry Glass. Henry Glass. Henry Glass played what? The air or bass? Uh... Bass drum.
And who was that? Buck, you said?

Bucku. Bucku. My name is Bucku. What did he play? Bass Trouba. Bass Trouba. And Archie was on trombone. Archie, he's gone. There he is. Archie Robertson. Trombone player. Oh. Big Boy. Big Boy. Big Boy. Big Boy. Big Boy. Big Boy. Big Boy. What's your name? Tillman.
Tillman. Big Alright. Did he used to play with him?
He was playing saxton. He was playing grand bassituber now.
Tillman was playing saxton. Alright, I don't even know what I'm doing.

Saxton. What kind of a band was that? Did they play by head or music? Music and by head both. What kind of marches? Marches? Well, most of them got marches from what we call the banner band books. I'll get the name of the books. Bennett? Bennett, yeah. The red? Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. That's one of the numbers. But all they were listening, they had one or two of those little books, you know? Yeah. I think they're four in all. Yeah, yeah. I believe I have four of them around here. I still have them here somewhere. And that's what we played out. And some by mostly the jazz, you know, by head, you know.
They march. What kind of jazz would you play in the street?

Tunes. Regular tunes. Well, you wouldn't play slow tunes, huh? In the marching time. In the marching time. Maybe the same, maybe the faster tempo, that's all. According to the, you know, play music according to the steps. You walk fast, you play according to the time. That's the idea. That's where the bass band is done. Did you play any funeral marches? Oh, yeah, I played a lot. Oh, yeah, I'm out of that. A lot of that. I played a million. Would that be written out? Some of it written, yeah.
